indemnify.definition: To compensate someone for harm or loss. Essentially, promising to pay them back if your actions cost them money.
indemnify.example: If your dog damages the apartment, you indemnify the landlord for the repair costs.

force majeure.definition: Unforeseeable circumstances that prevent someone from fulfilling a contract (often called an 'act of God').
force majeure.example: A hurricane destroying a warehouse is a force majeure event that excuses a shipping delay.

severability.definition: A rule stating that if one part of a contract is illegal or unenforceable, the rest of the contract still stands.
severability.example: If a lease has an illegal late fee, severability means the rest of the lease is still valid.

arbitration.definition: A private process where a neutral person (an arbitrator) decides a dispute, instead of going to public court.
arbitration.example: You give up your right to sue the company in court and must use their arbitration process instead.

lien.definition: A legal right to keep possession of property belonging to another person until a debt owed by that person is discharged.
lien.example: A mechanic puts a lien on your car until you pay the repair bill.
